summary: New --ui-bg-field role, because form fields looked transparent in dark. Reported as 'inputs have no colour inside'. The cause is that the surface scale INVERTS between schemes: in light bg-base is the lightest value (#FFFFFF) and sunken the darkest, but in dark bg-base (#423E3A) is the LIGHTEST surface while surface (#2F2C29) and sunken (#282522) are darker. Input and the Multiselect trigger painted their fill with bg-base, so in dark a field sitting on a bg-base page was exactly its container's colour and read as a hole. No existing role could fix it, because a field must be RECESSED from whatever contains it and that means lighter in light and darker in dark — opposite directions on the same scale. --ui-bg-field is now brandable, derived as colors.bg in light and a step below the surface in dark, pinned in theme zero as neutral-100 and neutral-0, and audited against both text-primary and text-placeholder. Measures 17.17:1 / 5.93:1 in light and 15.53:1 / 7.54:1 in dark. Caught by the visual harness on exactly one case — input dark — which is the correct blast radius, since light was already white.

migration.manual: Any component painting a form field with bg-base should move to bg-field. Light is unchanged (both resolve to white in theme zero); dark fields become a recessed near-black well instead of matching the page.
